instantiated_cells.justification: Section 13.66 prohibits any person from engaging in lobbying as a lobbyist unless licensed under §13.63 and authorized under §13.65, requiring all paid lobbyists to register.
A lobbyist license under §13.63(1)(a) expires on December 31 of each even-numbered year, and principal registration under §13.64(2) likewise expires biennially — a 24-month cycle.

Although §13.695(2) addresses state agency filers, it is the only express change-notification deadline in the subchapter, requiring reporting of changes within 10 days; §13.64(3) otherwise requires only pre-activity written notice of new areas without a numeric deadline.

The lobbyist must obtain a separate license under §13.63(1)(a), the principal must file a separate registration statement under §13.64(1), and §13.65 requires a separate authorization for each principal — these are distinct filings for each party.
Section 13.63(1)(a) enumerates the contents of a lobbyist license application (signature, SSN, residence address, fee) and does not require submission of a photograph.

Section 13.621(3) provides that elective state officials, local officials, tribal officials, and legislative employees are not subject to §§13.63, 13.64, 13.65, 13.68, or 13.695 when acting in an official capacity.

Section 13.621(2) exempts an agency that files a statement under §13.695 (and named officials) from §§13.625, 13.63, 13.64, 13.65, and 13.68 — substituting the simpler §13.695 reporting regime for the full lobbyist/principal scheme.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: Wisconsin's statute sets no post-activity deadline by which a lobbyist must register; §13.63 and §13.66 require licensing BEFORE engaging in lobbying, and §13.64's 10-day/$500 trigger applies to principals, not lobbyists. There is no "days after first lobbying" figure for the lobbyist.
